title: Kernelized Parameter Sensitivity Atlases for Amortized Conditional Interpretability
abstract: arXiv:2610.12737v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Gradient-based attribution provides input-specific information about model parameters, but computing it via backpropagation for many samples is expensive, while static importance scores discard input dependence. We derive KPSA (Kernelized Parameter Sensitivity Atlas) from a block decomposition of the empirical neural tangent kernel. It measures normalized parameter-group sensitivity, embeds those sources in an explicit query space, and uses a lightweight kernel to estimate sensitivities for unseen inputs. We derive bounds that separate finite-source from irreducible representation error and give margin-based top-$k$ recovery. This paper studies two interpretability applications. Firstly, KPSA identifies parameter groups with high susceptibility to perturbations across vision, forecasting, and protein-modeling setups. Across a fivefold range of parameter budgets ($0.02$-$0.1\%$), its selected groups attain $39$-$85\%$ of the perturbation

translated_title: 面向摊销式条件可解释性的核化参数敏感性图谱
translated_abstract: 基于梯度的归因方法能够提供关于模型参数的输入特定信息，但通过反向传播为大量样本计算归因代价高昂，而静态重要性得分则丢弃了对输入的依赖性。我们从经验神经正切核的分块分解出发推导出 KPSA（核化参数敏感性图谱）。它度量归一化的参数组敏感性，将这些敏感性来源嵌入一个显式的查询空间，并使用轻量级的核函数为未见过的输入估计敏感性。我们推导了区分有限来源误差与不可约表示误差的理论界，并给出了基于间隔（margin）的 top-k 恢复保证。本文研究了两个可解释性应用。其一，KPSA 在视觉、时序预测和蛋白质建模等多种设置中识别出对扰动高度敏感的参数组。在参数预算跨越五倍范围（0.02%–0.1%）的情况下，其选定的参数组可达到扰动效果的 39%–85%（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出 KPSA，通过经验神经正切核的分块分解构建参数组敏感性的核化图谱，用轻量级核函数摊销式地为任意新输入估计敏感性，从而以远低于逐样本反向传播的成本实现输入条件化的模型可解释性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes KPSA, which derives a kernelized atlas of parameter-group sensitivities from a block decomposition of the empirical neural tangent kernel, enabling amortized input-conditional interpretability and identification of perturbation-susceptible parameter groups at a fraction of the cost of per-sample backpropagation.
